elena: FYI we found ~1200 ciphertext blobs in partner-backups that are still wrapped with the old KMS key (key-id: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/partner/cryptoKeys/old-wrap). We need an eviction + rewrap plan + audit backfill. Won't be a silent sweep, coordinating now.
ajay: what's the blast radius? prod? staging? partners? :eyes:
elena: primary: staging backups (stg-backups), analytics-archive (read-only), and a handful of Vault transit prefixes used by partner-onboard. Not active writes from prod, but partner ingest might have replays.
sam: can we do a safe path: disable key for new encrypts, run decrypt+rewrap for blobs we own, then rotate Vault transit key and reconfigure consumers? Needs order.
leo: agree. sequence I propose: 1) add RBAC deny for encrypt on old key 2) enable audit sink for KMS accesses 3) run canary rewrap on 30 blobs 4) verify checksums + app-level acceptance 5) mass rewrap 6) scheduled key destroy/disable window.
elena: yes. Also need audit backfill for the last 90 days for any decrypt calls and who invoked them. We should surface any unusual principal.
ajay: who's owning the scripts? I can take the rewrap tooling if someone confirms the list of blob IDs + service accounts.
sam: elena can you dump the blob manifest and ACLs? I'll prep a `rewrap` script that uses `gcloud kms decrypt` -> `gcloud kms encrypt` to new key then updates metadata. Example snippet: ```bash
# decrypt then encrypt
gcloud kms decrypt --ciphertext-file=blob.cipher --location=global --keyring=partner --key=old-wrap --plaintext-file=blob.plain
gcloud kms encrypt --plaintext-file=blob.plain --location=global --keyring=partner --key=new-wrap --ciphertext-file=blob.rewrapped
```
elena: uploading manifest to S3: s3://redwood-security/tmp/partner-blob-manifest-1772345678.csv. Columns: blob_id, bucket, obj_path, last_access, owner_sa. Shared to @ajay @sam @leo.
leo: audit requirements: we need a backfill that shows: timestamp, principal, operation (encrypt/decrypt), resource name, and correlation-id. I'll coordinate with infra-logging to pull KMS audit logs into the security bucket and run a 90d query.
ajay: small ops note: while old key is disabled for encrypt we should still allow decrypt for a short window to rewrap. So RBAC change should deny `cloudkms.cryptoKeys.encrypt` but keep `decrypt` for the rewrap-runner SA.
sam: good call. We'll add explicit binding: `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` only to `rewrap-runner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for old key. Then after rewraps complete, revoke decrypt as well.
elena: can someone run a canary today around 18:00 UTC? Need to validate Vault transit rewrap behavior too (some secrets are via Vault -> KMS).
ajay: I can run the canary at 18:00 UTC. Plan: pick 30 blobs from manifest where last_access < 30d. Verify app-level reads for analytics.
leo: audit-bot: run KMS-access-query for key=old-wrap window=90d and dump to s3://redwood-security/audit-backfill/1772345678.json
audit-bot: queued KMS audit query (job id: kb-1772345678). Expect results in ~25m.
elena: escalation path: if canary fails (errors > 1%), we abort and rollback RBAC changes and restore encrypt permission. We'll pause production-triggered jobs until validated.
ajay: note on Vault: for transit wrapped secrets we must update `vault write transit/keys/new-wrap` and perform `vault write transit/rewrap` call. Sam, can you add a step to test rewrap on a test secret?
sam: will do. Example Vault rewrap call: ```bash
vault write transit/rewrap name=partner-transit ciphertext="<old-cipher>"
```
leo: timeline: today: canary + audit query. Tomorrow: mass rewrap (1am UTC maintenance window) unless canary shows issues. Post-mass: remove decrypt on old key and schedule destruction flags per compliance.
elena: owners: ajay (rewrap runner + canary), sam (vault transit rewrap + scripts), leo (audit backfill + RBAC changes), elena (incident lead + PM).
ajay: I'll create the rewrap runbook and post the run commands + expected logs in this thread before 17:30 UTC.
sam: I'll create a small harness to rewrap Vault secrets and run unit checks.
leo: I'll share the audit query results when done. If we see unexpected principals, we block mass rewrap and open a triage.
elena: thanks team. tagging CS.sg for partner comms: @sam please prep a short note we can send to partner Slack/ops if their ingest pipelines will be impacted. :shipit:
sam: drafting now, will ping for review.
leena: (typo) — ignore
audit-bot: KMS audit query kb-1772345678 completed. Results: 47 decrypt ops, 9 encrypt ops over 90d. Uploaded to s3://redwood-security/audit-backfill/1772345678.json
leo: pulling results now. Will summarize any non-standard principals in 10m.
ajay: prepping canary list and tests. Posting runbook shortly.
elena: leave a note here if you need temporary elevated access to run rewraps; we'll approve `rewrap-runner` SA creation and scoping now.
ajay: runbook posted: s3://redwood-security/runbooks/rewrap-runbook-1772345678.md. Canary scheduled 18:00 UTC.
sam: vault rewrap test passed on test-secret-002. Good to go for canary.
leo: audit summary: 3 decrypts from an outdated partner CI SA — I'll open a follow-up ticket to rotate that SA and notify partner. No other anomalies.
elena: proceeding with canary at 18:00 UTC. If all green, schedule mass run tomorrow 01:00 UTC.
ajay: canary done: 30/30 rewraps OK, checksum matches, analytics-nightly read OK. No errors. Full run scheduled. :thumbsup: 
sam: vault transit canary also OK.
leo: audit backfill confirmed no active external decrypts post-canary. ready for mass.
elena: thanks. Post-mass we'll revoke old decrypt and document on the compliance ticket.
